glance: Bitcoin plunged to about $55,000 Saturday, its lowest in two years, before bouncing back near $60,000 as liquidations topped $1 billion.
Mexico captured cartel boss Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, one of the FBI's most wanted; at least 11 died in ensuing clashes in Sinaloa.
The SEC is reportedly probing Nvidia's accounting after the stock fell 14% Friday, capping a seven-week, 44% slide.
CrowdStrike is said to be in talks to buy Zscaler, a deal that would create a roughly $265 billion security giant.
Wall Street ended its worst week since April 2025, with the S&P 500 and Dow in correction territory.

tech.headline: SEC reportedly probing Nvidia's accounting as the stock's slide deepens
tech.summary: Regulators are examining Nvidia's accounting practices, including a change last year in how it reports revenue by geography, according to Reuters sources. The news landed on a day Nvidia closed down 14%, its seventh straight weekly decline and a 44% drop over seven weeks, the longest losing streak since the 2008 crisis. The company is already without founder Jensen Huang, who resigned Nov 12, and faces a California subpoena.

tech.headline: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler
tech.summary: CrowdStrike is negotiating to buy rival Zscaler, Bloomberg reported Friday, a deal that would combine two of the largest cloud security firms into a company worth about $265 billion. Zscaler shares jumped more than 15% after hours. It would be one of the biggest tech deals of the year, arriving in the middle of a sharp market selloff.

tech.headline: Amazon: China-linked hackers ran autonomous AI agents in attacks
tech.summary: Amazon's threat intelligence team said China-nexus actors used an AI agent framework to autonomously find and exploit a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label, an open-source medical imaging tool, in a campaign against East Asian universities. It is one of the clearest documented cases of AI agents carrying out intrusions largely on their own. Separately this week, hackers breached a USDA farmer-payment system, NBC reported.

tech.headline: Claude-assisted Riemann hypothesis proof claim compiles but is unverified
tech.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge posted a claimed proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis produced with Claude and written in the Lean proof language; an MIT mathematician reports the code compiles, but no expert has yet understood or accepted it. Earlier this week Anthropic's research model raised the proven share of zeta zeros on the critical line from 41.6% to 67.2%, which mathematicians called notable but not a route to the full conjecture.

tech.headline: Intuit sells Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion
tech.summary: Bending Spoons, the Italian owner of Evernote, Vimeo and AOL, agreed to buy Mailchimp from Intuit for $3.68 billion, with Intuit reinvesting about $368 million. Intuit paid $12 billion for the email marketing firm in 2021 and says it will focus on AI-native tools for small businesses.

tech.headline: Trump threatens tax on US data centers built overseas
tech.summary: President Trump said he would bar US companies from building data centers abroad or hit them with a steep tax if they do. The threat adds to policy uncertainty for AI infrastructure spending, which has been at the center of this month's tech-stock rout.

tech.headline: Private AI valuations keep climbing: Databricks, Cognition seek funds
tech.summary: Databricks is in early talks to raise several billion dollars at about a $225 billion valuation, up from $190 billion in August, the WSJ reported, and Cognition is weighing a $2 billion-plus raise at $75 billion. Meanwhile Anthropic's newly public shares slid for a second day Friday but held above the $83 IPO price after a greenshoe lifted its raise to about $93.5 billion.

markets.asOf: market close, Nov 20 (markets closed for the weekend)
markets.summary: An AI-led selloff sent the S&P 500 down for a seventh straight day and into a correction, capping Wall Street's worst week since April 2025; the rout spilled into crypto over the weekend.

other.headline: Bitcoin briefly sinks to $55,000, a two-year low
other.summary: The selloff in tech stocks spread to crypto Saturday, with Bitcoin dropping to roughly $55,000 for the first time in two years before recovering to around $60,000. More than $1 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated during the plunge.

other.headline: Mexico captures cartel leader 'El Chapo Isidro'; 11 killed in Sinaloa
other.summary: Mexican forces arrested Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, a cartel boss on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, in an operation that used US intelligence. Seven alleged gunmen and four soldiers were killed in a firefight that began Friday night.

other.headline: Russian strikes hit Kryvyi Rih after deadly attacks on Kyiv and Lviv
other.summary: A ballistic missile attack on Zelenskyy's hometown overnight killed two and wounded about 60, damaging a hospital and schools, a day after strikes in Kyiv and Lviv killed at least 10. A Russian cargo ship caught fire in the Gulf of Finland after a drone hit, and Finland's prime minister warned the war is spilling into the region.

other.headline: YouTube nears $3 billion settlement with school districts
other.summary: YouTube reached an agreement in principle to pay about $3 billion to US school districts that accused it of fostering addiction among students, Bloomberg reported. Finalizing the deal could take months.

other.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin pledge to reduce nuclear risk
other.summary: The three leaders committed to steps aimed at lowering the danger of nuclear conflict, though the pledge left the war in Ukraine unresolved.

other.headline: World Court rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
other.summary: The International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority, a landmark ruling in the case brought by Gambia.
